title: Life Cycles of Plants
seo_title: Primary 3 Science: Life Cycles of Plants Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 3: Cycles in plants and animals (Life cycles of plants)
standard_text: Show an understanding that different plants have different life cycles: seed, germination, seedling, young plant, adult plant, flowers and fruits with seeds. Investigate the conditions needed for seeds to germinate: water, air and a suitable temperature (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on life cycles of plants: seed, germination, seedling, adult plant, flowers and fruits, with germination experiments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A seed grows into a plant that makes new seeds.
key_sub: Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.
body_html:
How to think about it

A flowering plant grows through stages: seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant → flowers → fruits with seeds.

  • A seed germinates when it has water, air and warmth. It does not need light or soil.
  • The young root grows out first. The seed leaves give food until the green leaves can make food.
  • The adult plant makes flowers. The flowers become fruits with seeds, and the cycle starts again.
  • Different plants take different times to complete their life cycles.
Example

Seeds on dry cotton wool did not germinate. Why?

Compare with the wet cotton wool

Only the water was different

Answer: They had no water.

Example

Seeds germinated in a dark cupboard. What does this show?

The seeds had water, air and warmth

They had no light

Answer: Light is not needed to germinate.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking seeds need soil to germinate. They have stored food, so wet cotton wool is enough.
  • Thinking seeds need light to germinate. Light is needed later, by the leaves.
  • Thinking the shoot comes out first. The root comes out first.
  • Changing two things at once in a germination experiment.

faq.q: What does a seed need to germinate?
faq.a: Water, air and a suitable temperature (warmth). It does not need light or soil, because it has food stored inside.

faq.q: Which part comes out of a seed first?
faq.a: The young root comes out first and grows downwards. Then the young shoot grows upwards.

faq.q: Do all plants have the same life cycle length?
faq.a: No. A green bean plant can make seeds in about two months, but a durian tree takes many years.

c: when a fruit falls from a tree
when a seed starts to grow into a new plant
items.e: The young root and shoot grow out of the seed.

items.q: What does a flowering plant make after its flowers?
items.e: The flowers develop into fruits that contain seeds.

Yes, but only in the day.

items.e: Once the stored food is used up, the leaves must make food.

items.q: Which statement about plant life cycles is correct?
c: Different plants take different lengths of time to complete their life cycles.
Trees have the shortest life cycles.
Plants with big seeds always grow fastest.
items.e: A bean plant takes weeks; a durian tree takes years.

items.q: A balsam plant takes about 3 months to grow from a seed to a plant that makes seeds. A mango tree takes about 5 years. Which has the longer life cycle?
items.e: Different plants take different lengths of time to complete their life cycles.

items.q: Where does a germinating seed get its food before it has green leaves?

items.e: That is why seeds can germinate without soil.

items.q: Why do the seed leaves of a bean seedling shrivel after a few days?
c: Their stored food is used up by the growing seedling.
They are eaten by the roots.
items.e: The green leaves then make food for the plant.

items.q: Which part of the seed protects it?

items.q: A mango seed and a balsam seed were planted at the same time. Which will make fruits first?
